slides.title: What does your mask protect you from?

body.text: This is scoring quick touches before a hug.

items: The touch player wins with three sets of two touches in a row.
The clinch player wins by closing his own hands around the touch player, under both elbows or chest to back.

body.text: This is getting past his legs and feet.

items: The top player wins by touching the backs of both of the bottom player's knees with his shin, one and then the other.
The bottom player wins by making the top player sit down, then sitting up himself.

body.text: This is sitting on top of his belly.

items: The top player holds as long as he keeps an arm under one of the bottom player's elbows.
The bottom player wins by touching both elbows to his body, or making the top player fall.

slides.title: What made it work?
slides.question: Tonight you got past his legs while he lay on his back. What got you in?

options.text: Your shin stepping behind his knee.
options.feedback: His legs protect his body, the way a mask protects what is under it.

options.text: Jumping over both of his legs.
options.feedback: Jumping gives his feet a chance to push you.
His head is not where the gap is.

body.text: Tonight you worked from the hand fight, open guard, and mount. Your guard protects your legs, and your mask protects something in you. Naming what your mask guards is the same skill as naming what a guard defends. You get to use your mask on purpose.
